title: The full cohomological-dimension condition on the blueprint's coefficient class
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$,
$A=A_{E,n}$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, finite-type $k$-schemes $Y$
and $\overline X$ with $\dim\overline X\leq d$
([def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]) and a proper finite-type
morphism $p:\overline X\to Y$. Then the vanishing required by
[def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] holds for every coefficient
sheaf of the blueprint's class [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], with the
bound $c=2d$ and uniformly over all base changes $V\to Y$ of
$Y_{\Proet}$; that is,

$$
\mathcal H^r\bigl(R(p_V)_*(\mathcal F|_{\overline X\times_YV})\bigr)=0
\qquad(r>2d)
$$

for every base change $V\to Y$ and every $\mathcal F$ of that class.
Moreover that class is closed under inverse image along morphisms of
finite-type $k$-schemes, under extensions and under colimits, and it
contains the constant coefficient sheaf and every sheaf of étale origin.

proof.text: Fix a sheaf $\mathcal F$ in the class and choose its defining witness $\mathcal F\cong\nu_{\overline X}^*G$ with $G$ an étale $A$-module sheaf [def-sf-fullcd-used-class]. The coefficient ring $A$ is finite [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. In particular some positive integer $N$ kills $1_A$ (two terms of the sequence $0,1_A,2\cdot1_A,\ldots$ coincide), and hence kills every section of every $A$-module sheaf. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$ is torsion, even when $G$ is not constructible or finite. We use only the essential image of $\nu^*$, not all pro-étale sheaves.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: identify the coefficient class and torsion hypothesis

proof.text: The absolute clause of [thm-sf-fullcd-etale-origin] gives $\mathcal H^r(Rp_{\Proet,*}\nu_{\overline X}^*G)=0$ for $r>2d$. Here the hypotheses are the original finite-type $k$-schemes, algebraically closed $k$, proper finite-type $p$, and $\dim\overline X\leq d$. This step uses no base-change clause of that theorem.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: the absolute vanishing clause

proof.text: Both $p$ and each $p_V$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Indeed $p_V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; a proper morphism is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its diagonal is a closed immersion: the inverse image of an affine open under that diagonal is affine, hence quasi-compact, by the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is exactly quasi-separatedness [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The same reasoning applies to $p$. No finite-type-over-$k$ hypothesis on $V$ is used.

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $p$ and $G[0]$ to get $Rp_{\Proet,*}
u_{\overline X}^*G\cong
u_Y^*Rp_{\Et,*}G$. The comparison inverse image is exact and the unit $M	o

proof.text: For the coefficient-forgetting calculations use the module-valued encoding via [lem-weil-pbc-etale-constant-ring-module-equivalence], which keeps the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged. The equivalence is exact; it transports injective resolutions, since the defining extension property for an injective object is unchanged under an exact equivalence. Direct images correspond because both have sections on $U$ equal to sections over the inverse-image object. Thus their derived cohomology corresponds as well. Let $v:V\to Y$ be any object of $Y_{\Proet}$ and write $g:\overline X_V\to\overline X$ for the other projection. Put $B$ equal to the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies $\mathcal H^r(Rp_*B[0])$ with the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^rp_*G$, so it vanishes for $r>2d$ by Step 4. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the cartesian square $(g,p_V,p,v)$ and $B[0]$, which has torsion cohomology by Step 1. It gives $R(p_V)_{\Et,*}g^{-1}B\cong v^{-1}Rp_{\Et,*}B$. Since $v^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], cohomology on the right is $v^{-1}\mathcal H^r(Rp_{\Et,*}B)=0$ for $r>2d$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-pullback-forget-modules], $g^{-1}B$ is the underlying abelian sheaf of $g_{\Et}^*G$. Apply [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] to $p_V$; faithfulness and exactness of forgetting modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] now give $R^r(p_V)_{\Et,*}g_{\Et}^*G=0$. Indeed if the underlying sheaf of a module object is zero, its identity is zero, and the object is zero. This argument imposes no dimension or finite-type condition on $V$.

source.place: Tag 095T, theorem-proper-base-change; exact inverse image and the cited coefficient-forgetting comparisons

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $g_{\Proet}^*\mathcal F\cong
u_{\overline X_V}^*(g_{\Et}^*G)$, with the same constant coefficient ring $A$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to the qcqs morphism $p_V$ (Step 3) and the degree-zero sheaf $g_{\Et}^*G$. Its right derived image is $
u_V^*R(p_V)_{\Et,*}g_{\Et}^*G$. Exactness of $
u_V^*$ [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] commutes with cohomology as in Step 4; Step 5 therefore gives $\mathcal H^r(R(p_V)_{\Proet,*}g_{\Proet}^*\mathcal F)=0$ for $r>2d$. This is the relative clause of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] restricted to the stated coefficient class; Step 2 is the absolute clause. The integer $2d$ is unchanged for every $V$.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison, and the commuting square immediately preceding it; restricted FullCD conclusion

proof.text: If $h:T'\to T$ is a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes and $\mathcal F\cong\nu_T^*G$, then [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] gives $h_{\Proet}^*\mathcal F\cong\nu_{T'}^*(h_{\Et}^*G)$. The sheaf $h_{\Et}^*G$ is an étale $A$-module sheaf by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. This is an étale-origin witness on $T'$ [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], so the class is stable under inverse image.

proof.text:
For colimits fix a small category $J$ and a diagram $H:J	o\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A)$ whose values are of étale origin. By the unit isomorphism [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] and the adjunction triangle identity [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], the counit $\epsilon_{H_j}:
u_T^*
u_{T,*}H_j	o H_j$ is an isomorphism for each $j$. Explicitly, for an origin isomorphism $\alpha_j:
u_T^*G_j\xrightarrow{\sim}H_j$ and unit $\eta$, the triangle identity gives $\epsilon_{
u_T^*G_j}=(
u_T^*\eta_{G_j})^{-1}$, and counit naturality gives $\epsilon_{H_j}=\alpha_j\circ(
u_T^*\eta_{G_j})^{-1}\circ
u_T^*
u_{T,*}(\alpha_j^{-1})$. Each factor is invertible. Counit naturality makes these into an isomorphism of diagrams, so no incompatible choices of lifts of arrows are involved. The diagram $
u_{T,*}H$ has a colimit $G$ in étale $A$-module sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Since $
u_T^*$ is a left adjoint [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] identifies $\operatorname{colim}_J H\cong
u_T^*G$. This witnesses closure under all small colimits, including the empty colimit.

proof.text:
The constant coefficient sheaf is also in the class. The constant $A$-module sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] represents the functor of global sections: a map $A_T	o M$ is determined by the image of $1$, and every global section defines such a map by scalar multiplication and sheafification. By the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], maps $
u_T^*(A_{T,\Et})	o M$ correspond to global sections of $
u_{T,*}M$. Restriction to étale objects leaves the terminal object $T$ unchanged, so these are exactly the global sections of $M$. The natural universal properties therefore identify $
u_T^*(A_{T,\Et})\cong A_{T,\Proet}$ (the two representing maps induced by $1$ compose to the identities). Finally every sheaf of étale origin belongs to the class by its defining witness [def-sf-fullcd-used-class].

The level n+1 parametrizes exactly all positive levels. All closure and containment clauses use the same essential-image predicate, with no constructibility or sheaf-finiteness restriction.
